title: Alternative causal orientations in the cell-bridge class
legend: The cell-bridge class contains three distinct directed acyclic graphs, reproduced from the frozen candidate-DAG enumeration. Estimated genome size -> cell area -> nucleus area, its reverse chain, and cell area -> both traits all imply genome–nucleus conditional independence given cell area. These orientations are statistically indistinguishable in this three-trait comparison; their common conditional structure is the supported result.
alt_text: Three equally compatible DAGs show genome to cell to nucleus, the reverse chain, and cell area pointing to both genome and nucleus.

title: Primary comparison of ten path classes
legend: Ten testable path-equivalence classes are ranked by CICc using 24 species, standardized log10 traits, the supplied dated tree and Pagel-lambda regressions. The cell-bridge class has CICc = 13.3829, Fisher C = 0.04959, one independence claim, global-fit P = 0.97551, and relative weight = 0.91674. Its tested claim is the residual genome–nucleus association after conditioning on cell area (P = 0.97551). All nine other tested classes fail the P >= 0.05 global-fit criterion; the nucleus-bridge class has delta CICc = 13.77171 and global-fit P = 0.0009971. Weights compare only the supplied ten classes; six saturated DAGs impose no testable d-separation claim and are not ranked. All primary component regressions have fitted lambda approximately 1e-7. No direction-specific coefficients are assigned to the winning equivalence class.
alt_text: Ten models are ranked by delta CICc; only cell bridge passes global fit, with weight 0.917. Nucleus bridge is 13.77 units behind.

title: Marginal and conditional genome–cellular associations
legend: Released S28 Pagel-lambda coefficients compare marginal and conditional associations, with standardized log10 traits and estimated genome size as predictor in all four regressions. The genome–nucleus coefficient is 0.41902 (95% normal interval 0.03960 to 0.79844) marginally, and 0.00792 (-0.49195 to 0.50780) after adjusting for cell area. The genome–cell coefficient is 0.71666 (0.42523 to 1.00810) marginally, and 0.57486 (0.27994 to 0.86977) after adjusting for nucleus area. Intervals are the stored S28 normal approximations (coefficient +/- 1.96 standard errors), not the t intervals used for the Figure 5 pairwise displays. The adjusted genome–nucleus P is 0.97551; the adjusted genome–cell P is 0.0009971. These estimates explain the contrasting independence tests but are not estimates of indirect causal effects. The broad adjusted genome–nucleus interval does not establish an exactly zero effect. No models were refitted and these coefficients are not labelled on the three equivalent DAG orientations.
alt_text: Genome–nucleus coefficient decreases from 0.419 to 0.008 after adjusting for cell area, whereas genome–cell decreases from 0.717 to 0.575 after adjusting for nucleus area.

title: Path-class ranking across sensitivity analyses
legend: Cell bridge ranks first in 246/250 measurement resamples, 24/24 leave-one-species-out fits, 4/4 evolutionary-model specifications and 200/200 published-tree fits. The first and third checks retain 24 species, species omission retains 23 per fit, and the published-tree analysis contains only 18 species. All 200 published-tree fits also retain nucleus bridge as globally admissible and within delta CICc <= 2, so top ranking does not indicate unique support. On the focal tree pruned to the same 18 species, cell-bridge weight is 0.43357 and nucleus-bridge weight is 0.32240 (delta CICc = 0.59252); the published main tree gives essentially the same values. These reduced-species results primarily expose dependence of discrimination on taxon coverage, rather than establishing strong topology robustness.
alt_text: Cell bridge ranks first in 246 of 250 resamples, all 24 omissions, all four evolutionary models, and all 200 trees. The 18-species tree fits also support nucleus bridge.
